The pure breeze harmonized with profound virtue,
sincere transformation flowed with nature.
Following the ancient sages and aligning with their tracks,
he always reflected thrice to consider faults.
Summoning the virtuous from obscurity,
opening the path for bold remonstrance and honest speech.
Inviting the pure and upright from secluded gardens,
presenting bundles of silk as gifts.
High and low communicated their sentiments,
feasting together in joy and delight.
"When it came time to sacrifice at the suburban altar to Heaven,
to repay the earth's bounty,
to pray for blessings from the supreme mystery,
he contemplated how to show reverence.
The solemn rituals were fully performed,
the reverent ceremonies exhaustively carried out.
Then, with utmost sincerity offered,
presenting the pure sacrifice,
it was said: 'Truly,
this is the Son of Heaven.'
He then arranged his ritual robes,
straightened his crown and sash.
With pendants, tassels, and ribbons,
jade hairpins and fastenings.
Fire and dragon patterns, embroidered emblems,
adorned with tassels and hanging ornaments.
Tying the flying-cloud carriage canopy,
erecting the tall canopy with kingfisher feathers.
Raising the grand banner with twelve pendants,
fluttering and swaying gracefully.
Six black dragons, majestic and splendid,
prancing together with vigor and grace.
Dragon-prowed chariots with ornate yokes,
gold-inlaid and engraved bridles.
Square cheekpieces and left-side plumes,
breastplates hooked and adorned with jade.
The tinkling of bells harmonious,
the ringing of harmonious chimes clear.
Double wheels and reinforced axles,
spoked hubs and flying linchpins.
Feathered canopies lush and drooping,
floral ornaments on curved stems.
Adorning according to the season with supplementary attire,
all with dragon banners and numerous tassels.
Standing halberds slanting with blades,
agricultural carriages and wooden carts.
Ninety-nine attendant chariots,
carriages and chariots moving side by side.
Crossbows and layered banners,
vermilion streamers and blue canopies.
After the escort was arranged,
the vanguard chariots set forth.
Phoenix banners and leather-covered vehicles,
plain silk and deep-red pennants.
Cloud-patterned nets and nine-streamered flags,
halberds and spears densely arrayed.
Horsemen with embroidered robes,
tiger warriors wearing pheasant feathers.
Harnessing the Púshāo horses from Chénghuá,
flying tassels swaying elegantly.
Gathering light infantry in the rear formation,
sounding the war drums with roaring clamor.
Warriors in armor brandishing their weapons,
wearing golden bells and raising yellow battle-axes.
Clearing the road and arranging the ranks,
moving like stars across the sky.
Solemn and orderly,
rumbling and rumbling steadily.
Before the rear guard had left the city gates,
the banners had already returned to the suburban borders.
Emulating the utmost beauty of the great Xià,
showing reverence and respect to the bright spirits.
"Then came the bamboo pipes of Gūzhú,
the cloud-harmony zithers.
Thunder drums booming deeply,
after six changes were completed.
Wearing floral crowns and holding pheasant feathers,
dancers arranged in eight rows.
The great sacrifice was duly performed,
all the revered spirits received their proper offerings.
Raising the blazing smoke of the piled firewood,
sending high smoke to the Great Unity.
The spirits enjoyed the fragrance and regarded his virtue,
bestowing great fortune upon the sacred ruler.
Then he honored the Supreme Deity in the Bright Hall,
elevating Emperor Guāngwǔ to accompany him.
Distinguishing the directions and correcting the norms,
the five essences led and came forth.
Honoring the red brilliance of the Chìshì,
the four numinous creatures responded with sincere embrace.
Thus, as spring and autumn changed seasons,
the four times alternated in succession.
With a heart full of devotion,
moved by things, he deepened his thoughts.
Personally pursuing nourishment at the ancestral temple,
presenting the winter and autumn sacrifices, along with the summer and spring offerings.
Examining the sacrificial animals carefully,
setting up the restraining yoke.
Roasted whole pig and sliced meat,
also with harmonious broth.
Cleansed pure and exquisite,
the rituals brilliantly clear.
The myriad dances grand and splendid,
bells and drums resounding loudly.
The numinous ancestors and imperial father,
came to behold and partake.
The spirits, all intoxicated, rested,
bestowing abundant blessings."
"When the Farmer's Star appears at dawn in its proper position,
the fertile soil begins to pulse with life.
Riding in the imperial carriage drawn by azure dragons,
between the drivers, he grasps the sharp plowshare.
He personally pushes the plow three times in the celestial field,
cultivating the thousand acres of the imperial domain.
To provide the sacrificial grains for the Di and suburban rites,
he must devote his thoughts to diligent self-exertion.
The myriad people are encouraged in the fields,
moved to exert their strength in weeding and nurturing the sprouts.
In the warm spring sunlight,
archery is held together at the Pìyōng.
The stands and racks are set up,
the palace bells and golden chimes are suspended.
The war drums and hand drums,
with feathered banners standing tall.
Thus all things are prepared,
each with its proper form.
Bóyí rises to oversee the ceremony,
while Hòukuí sits to direct the music.
The great target is set up,
marked with the five colors.
Three shelters are arranged,
and officials are stationed with flags.
The arrow-retrieving tools are set,
stored in the vast courtyard.
Then the imperial carriage sets out early,
arriving at the eastern steps,
waiting for the dawn to break.
Sweeping away the morning clouds,
ascending to the light of heaven at Fúsāng.
The Son of Heaven then grasps the jade-adorned carriage,
timely riding the six dragons.
The whale-shaped drumstick strikes,
the ornate bell resounds.
Dàbǐng reins in the pace,
Fēnghòu accompanies the ride.
Shètí steers the chariot,
slowly arriving at the archery palace.
Ritual affairs are displayed,
musical instruments are readied.
The 'Wáng Xià' concludes,
the 'Zōu Yú' is played.
Thumb rings and arm guards are donned in order,
the carved bows are drawn.
Releasing the remaining shoots in late spring,
manifesting sincerity to convey afar.
Advancing bright virtue and honoring achievements,
cleansing the gluttonous greed.
Benevolent winds spread and flow outward,
righteous principles stir and reach far.
The sun and moon meet at Lóngmáng,
sympathizing with the toil of the people's affairs.
Taking advantage of rest to relieve labor,
bringing joy with spring wine.
Holding the ceremonial knife to bare and carve,
offering wine and beans to the elders of the state.
Descending from supreme dignity to teach humility,
bowing in greeting and farewell to the three elders.
Reverently cautious in dignified demeanor,
showing the people not to be negligent. I have esteemed guests,
their joy is profound.
The influence of teachings spreads,
filling the celestial realm.
"When civil virtue is made manifest,
martial discipline is proclaimed.
In the intervals of the three farming seasons,
displaying might in the central plains.
In the midwinter month,
a grand review is held in the Western Garden.
The gamekeeper is in charge,
preparing in advance.
Gathering all kinds of birds,
assembling them in the spiritual park.
Where the beasts congregate,
it is called readiness reported.
Then he mounts the light chariot,
steering the nimble carriage.
Four stallions in the hunt,
both sturdy and well-trained.
Spears and halberds like a forest,
commander's banners fluttering densely.
Reaching Shànglín Park,
forming camps with followers.
Setting up markers in harmony,
the bell officer hands out gongs.
Sitting, rising, advancing, retreating,
regulated by military sounds.
Orders repeated thrice, commands given five times,
demonstrating execution by slaughtering animals.
Deploying troops and addressing the ranks,
instructions conveyed, prohibitions established.
Fire signals all raised,
warriors spread like stars.
Formations like geese, cranes, fish scales,
spread like winnowing fans, extended like wings.
Wheel dust covers the tracks,
neither hasty nor slow.
Driving without deceitful encounters,
shooting without cutting fur.
Presenting six kinds of game as offerings,
timely feasting on four types of fat.
Horses' hooves not pushed to the limit,
charioteers and foot soldiers not wearied.
Completing the ritual with three drives,
releasing nets, freeing unicorns.
Not indulging in pleasure to teach frugality,
not exhausting things to show benevolence.
Admiring Tiānyǐ's loosening of nets,
following teachings to cherish the people.
Emulating Jī Bó at Wèiyáng,
missing bears but gaining men.
Kindness moistens insects,
awe shakes the eight regions.
Fond of joy but not excessive,
truly civil, truly martial.
The modest hunt at Áo,
was trivial indeed.
The search at Qíyáng,
how could it be worth counting?
"Then at year's end, the great exorcism,
driving away all pestilences.
Fāngxiàng wields the battle-axe,
shamans and sorcerers hold brooms.
Ten thousand child exorcists,
red heads and black attire.
Peachwood bows and thorn arrows,
shot without missing the target.
Flying stones scatter like rain,
fierce plagues are surely slain.
Blazing torches race like shooting stars,
chasing red pestilence to the four borders.
Then soaring over the celestial pool,
crossing the flying bridge.
Striking down mountain demons,
beheading wild maniacs.
Chopping the serpentine creature,
smashing the head of Fāngliáng.
Imprisoning Gēngfù in the clear cold,
drowning Nǚbá in the divine marsh.
Destroying Kuíxū and Wǎngxiàng,
slaying Yězhòng and annihilating Yóuguāng.
The eight spirits tremble in fear,
let alone Jìyù and Bìfāng.
Dùshuò acts as a barrier,
guarded by Yùlǜ.
Shénshū assists him,
holding reed ropes facing each other.
Eyes inspecting every corner,
seizing leftover ghosts.
The capital's chambers are secure and pure,
with nothing amiss.
"Thus yin and yang harmoniously blend,
all things are timely nurtured.
Divining journeys and examining omens,
ultimately all is truly good.
The imperial carriage tours Dàiyuè,
encouraging farming on plains and hills.
Unifying measures, pitch pipes, and axle widths,
balancing urgency and ease with cold and warmth.
Inspecting the obscure and bright to promote or demote,
then turning the banners to return.
Gazing upon the former emperor's old ruins,
sighing with deep longing and cherishing antiquity!
Waiting for the west wind to journey far,
reverently sacrificing to Gāozǔ.
Already spring outings to stimulate growth,
awakening hibernating creatures from hidden doors.
In autumn excursions to celebrate harvest,
observing the abundant year's many grains.
Praising the field overseers' diligence,
bestowing rewards to the nine guardians.
Looking left to Yánggǔ,
glancing right to Xuánpǔ.
Gazing to the horizon's edge with distant hopes,
planning for ten thousand generations with grand designs.
Returning home to relieve fatigue,
receiving abundant blessings for peace and health.
Gathering all auspicious signs,
fully obtaining excellent omens.
Enclosing Línshì's Zōuyú,
taming marsh horses and Ténghuáng.
The singing Luánniǎo of Nǚchuáng,
the dancing Fènghuáng of Dānxué.
Planting Huápíng in spring gardens,
flourishing Zhūcǎo in central courtyards.
Kindly winds widely spread,
grace reaching distant wilderness.
Harmonizing Dīnglìng in the north,
pacifying Yuèshāng in the south.
Encompassing Dàqín in the west,
passing Lèlàng in the east.
Peoples of diverse tongues through nine translations,
all bow and come to pay homage as kings."
"Thus, when discussing the relocation of the capital and the change of the capital city,
it follows the model of the Pan Geng of the Shang dynasty.
Changing from extravagance to frugality,
it aligns with the beauty of the 'Sī Gàn'.
Ascending Mount Tài to perform the fēng sacrifice and descending to perform the shàn sacrifice,
it matches the virtue of Huángdì and Xuānyuán.
Acting without action,
engaging in affairs without affairs,
eternally possessing the people,
thereby achieving great peace.
Adhering to frugality,
valuing simplicity and plainness.
Reflecting on Confucius's self-restraint,
practicing Lǎozǐ's constant contentment.
So that the heart is not disturbed by its surroundings,
the eyes do not see what is desirable.
Devaluing rhinoceros horns and ivory,
simplifying pearls and jade.
Hiding gold in the mountains,
discarding jade discs in the valleys.
Kingfisher feathers are not torn,
tortoiseshell is not collected.
What is valued is only the worthy,
what is treasured is only grain.
The people abandon the trivial and return to the fundamental,
all cherish loyalty and uphold sincerity.
At this time,
the whole world rejoices together,
saying:
'Ah!
The virtue of the Hàn Emperor,
how magnificent it is!'
It is difficult to cultivate the míngjiá plant,
thus it is unseen for generations.
Only our sovereign can cultivate it,
leading to peace and harmony,
and it will soon be counted on the court steps.
Then how can the Way not be cherished,
how can transformation not be gentle?
Sound soars with the wind,
favor flows with the clouds.
All things rely on me,
what more is there to seek?
Virtue covers the heavens,
brilliance shines like light.
Surpassing the narrowness of the Three Sovereigns,
outstripping the long drive of the Five Emperors.
Following the distant footsteps of the Two Sovereigns,
who can say the carriage is slow and cannot keep up?
The beauty of the Eastern Capital is not fully expressed,
but I am afflicted with a minor illness,
unable to explore its details thoroughly.
Thus, I have roughly outlined its general idea for you, my guest.
"If one indulges in dissipation and forgets to return,
lets the mind wander unconsciously,
seeks pleasure without restraint,
later suffering calamity,
a single word nearly leads to the loss of the state,
this is something I have not learned.
Moreover, even with the wisdom of carrying a pitcher,
one guards it and does not lend the vessel.
How much more so when inheriting the imperial enterprise and轻视 the heavenly position.
Looking up to the two founders,
their achievements are vast and extensive.
Always trembling with fear and caution,
as if riding a galloping horse without reins.
The white dragon disguised as a fish,
was trapped by Yùjū.
Even the Son of Heaven, fearless as he may be,
still feels apprehension before a single commoner.
Never leaving his supply wagons all day,
how can he travel incognito alone?
The ruler of men,
stuffs yellow silk in his ears.
In the carriage, he does not look back.
Jade pendants regulate his demeanor,
carriage bells pace his journey.
His steps do not disturb the jade pendants,
his carriage does not break its stride.
Turning warhorses to pull manure carts,
why regret losing swift steeds like Yǎoniǎo and Fēitù?
When using wealth and acquiring goods,
he always fears the exhaustion of living things.
In levying taxes and assigning labor,
he always fears the depletion of human strength.
Acquiring through the Way,
using in due season.
Mountains are not stripped bare,
hunting does not target pregnant animals.
Plants and trees flourish luxuriantly,
birds and beasts multiply abundantly.
The people forget their toil,
gladly contribute their wealth.
The common folk share in abundance,
high and low enjoy harmony and prosperity together.
Vast grace is accumulated over time,
the people's hearts are firmly united.
Upholding righteousness and caring for the sovereign,
all cherish unwavering integrity.
Resenting treacherous villains who defy fate,
lamenting the imperial lineage being usurped,
secret plans were devised and executed covertly,
combining eighteen to form a stratagem.
Elevating the sage emperor to the heavenly steps,
manifesting the orderly reign of the Hàn dynasty.
Thus,
the royal enterprise can be joyful.
"Now, sir, if you merely delight in exploiting the people for fleeting pleasure,
forgetting that the people's resentment becomes enmity;
delight in exhausting resources for extreme favor,
neglecting that rebellion from below breeds worry.
Water is what carries the boat,
but also what can capsize it.
Solid ice begins with frost underfoot,
a towering tree starts from a sprout.
Diligence at dawn for great glory,
yet later generations still grow slack.
Moreover, if the initial system is overly extravagant,
how can those who follow it reform?
Thus, Sīmǎ Xiàngrú praised the spectacle of the Shànglín Park,
Yáng Xióng elaborated on the imperial hunt.
Although they concluded with tearing down walls and filling moats,
and ended with收起 nets and traps,
ultimately it did not aid moral instruction,
only revealed their faults.
Ministers overstepping to encroach upon the sovereign,
forgetting the long-term foundation of governing the state.
Thus, the watchman's clapper sounded east of Hángǔ Pass,
and the Western Court collapsed with none to uphold it.
Generally, what the human mind learns,
the body becomes accustomed to.
In a fish market, one does not notice the stench,
accustomed to what first enters.
The Xiánchí music does not match the crude tunes of wā yǎo,
yet some listeners may doubt it.
Who can remain unconfused?
Is it only Zǐyě?
The guest, already intoxicated by the great Way,
satiated with literary meaning,
encouraged by virtue and awed by warnings,
joy and fear contend within.
Dazed as if waking from drunkenness,
weary from morning till night,
spirit drained and soul stripped away,
forgetting what he was discussing,
losing what he was boasting about.
After a long while, he finally spoke:
How shallow I am!
Accustomed to error and thus led astray,
fortunate to have your guidance.
What I have heard,
is flashy but insubstantial;
your words, sir,
are trustworthy and well-founded.
I, an ignorant man,
from now on,
know that the virtuous fragrance of the great Hàn,
lies entirely herein.
I once regretted that the Three Fén and Five Diǎn were lost,
unable to witness the beauty of Yándì
and Dìkuí,
but having heard your additional discourse,
how could even Dàtíngshì surpass this?
Though I am not clever,
I hope to comprehend this.
Oh, illustrious joyful capital,
both beautiful and prosperous!
South of the secondary capital,
situated north of the Hàn River.
Carving out fertile lands of Zhōu and Chǔ,
spanning Jīng and Yù as its borders,
with a refreshing, elevated, and spacious terrain,
richly abundant and difficult to describe in detail.
As for its geographical features,
Wǔquè Pass guards its west,
Tóngbǎi Mountain marks its east.
The Cānglàng River flows as its moat,
the vast Fāngchéng forms its walls.
Tānggǔ springs surge behind it,
Yùshuǐ River washes its chest.
Pushing from the Huái, drawing from the Tuān,
connecting three directions.
As for its treasures, valuables, and rare wonders,
there are gold with colorful patterns and uncut jade,
the Suí Pearl and luminous night-shining gems.
Copper, tin, lead, and refined iron,
red ochre, white clay, and orpiment.
Green jasper, azurite, purple crystals,
blue mineral pigments, and cinnabar grains.
Tàiyǐ Yúliáng,
Zhōnghuáng Juéyù.
Sōngzǐ Shénbēi,
Chìlíng Jiějiǎo.
Gēngfù radiates light in the clear, cold abyss,
while the roaming maidens play with pearls at the bends of Hàngāo.
Its mountains are lofty and rugged,
steep and perilous.
Jagged and towering,
precipitous and towering high.
Deep valleys, sheer and towering,
hold frost and snow even in summer.
Some are connected in winding ranges,
while others are abruptly severed in the middle.
Soaring high, they hide the sky,
and looking down, one sees only clouds and rainbows.
As for Tiānfēng Dàhú,
it is a dwelling place for immortals.
The summit is flat, expansive, and open,
while the base is overgrown and rugged.
Slopes and ridges rise steeply like cauldrons,
and streams and gullies twist and wind intricately.
Mushroom-like growths thrive in its recesses,
and jade-like sap overflows in its corners.
Even Kūnlún cannot surpass it,
and Lángfēng cannot exceed it.
Its trees include tamarisk, pine, and wild jujube,
juniper, cypress, and oak.
Maple, boxwood, sumac, and oak,
and the mulberry tree of the Emperor's daughter.
Sago palm and betel palm,
wild mulberry, cudrania, and sandalwood.
Their roots are deep and trunks towering,
their branches hang gracefully.
They spread lush green leaves,
and display abundant blossoms and stamens.
Dark clouds gather, bringing deep shade,
and valley winds rise, adding to the sorrow.
They stand clustered and dense,
in deep blue obscurity.
Dense and flourishing in the valley depths,
towering and piercing the sky.
Tigers, leopards, and brown bears roam below,
while macaques and gibbons play on the peaks.
Phoenixes and simurghs soar above,
and swift monkeys and flying squirrels dwell among them.
Its bamboos include thick and slender varieties,
small and large kinds.
They spread along slopes and banks,
lush and variegated.
Luxuriant and dense,
swaying in the wind like clouds.
As for its rivers and streams,
they originate from rocky caves,
gushing forth from hidden sources.
Emerging from deep caverns,
flowing swiftly and turbulently.
Spreading widely and unrestrained,
vast and overflowing.
Converging and surging forward,
swift as arrows, rapid as the wind.
Torrents plunge into deep pools,
roaring and crashing.
Flowing far and wide,
clear and rapid.
Its aquatic creatures include giant turtles and singing snakes,
hidden dragons and lurking serpents.
Sturgeons and giant fish,
softshell turtles, crocodiles, and sharks.
Giant clams holding pearls,
and strange creatures coiling and winding.
In its marshes and lakes,
there are Qiánlú and Yùchí,
Zhěyáng and Dōngbēi.
Storing still waters,
stretching endlessly without bounds.
Its plants include reeds, ramie, and duckweed,
wild rice, cattails, and rushes.
Water weeds, water chestnuts, and lotus,
lotuses in full bloom.
Blossoming in the wind,
displaying fragrant flowers.
Its birds include mandarin ducks, swans, and egrets,
wild geese, bustards, and swan geese,
ducks and grebes,
and various waterfowl.
Chirping in harmonious songs,
floating gently on the waves.
Its waters are channeled and directed,
irrigating the rice fields.
Canals and ditches interconnected,
dikes and ridges linked together.
Even without morning clouds,
the marshes alone provide abundance.
When drained, they become dry land,
suitable for irrigation or farming.
Winter rice and summer wheat,
ripening in their seasons.
Its plains and fields grow mulberry, lacquer, hemp, and ramie,
beans, wheat, millet, and broomcorn.
A hundred grains flourish abundantly,
lush and thriving.
In its gardens and orchards,
there are knotweed, fishwort, and ginger lily,
yams, sugarcane, ginger, and garlic,
shepherd's purse, taro, and melons.
There are also cherries, plums, and mountain persimmons,
peaches, pears, and chestnuts.
Jujubes and pomegranates,
fragrant oranges and Dèng tangerines.
Its fragrant herbs include climbing fig, orchid, and indigo,
lovage, sweet flag, and angelica.
Dense and lush,
emitting rich fragrances.
As for its kitchen and feasts,
there are fragrant millet and fine glutinous rice,
and aromatic rice from Zhìgāo.
Returning wild geese and calling doves,
yellow rice and fresh fish,
prepared with spices.
Sweet, sour, and flavorful,
a hundred varieties, a thousand names.
Spring eggs and summer bamboo shoots,
autumn leeks and winter greens.
Perilla, prickly ash, and purple ginger,
removing any gamey odors.
The wine includes nine-brewed sweet liquor,
and ten-day clarified ale.
The fermented brew forms bubbles an inch wide,
floating like duckweed.
Its sweetness never cloys,
intoxicating but not causing hangovers.
And when gathering clans and comforting relatives,
for seasonal sacrifices and offerings,
to invite distant friends,
honored guests are welcomed.
Bowing and yielding, they ascend,
feasting in the orchid hall.
Rare delicacies and precious dishes,
fill round and square vessels.
Exquisitely carved and adorned,
with gold, silver, and gemstones.
Attendants are charming and graceful,
their attire bright and fresh.
Dressed in varied and intricate garments,
treading on embroidered shoes.
Quick-witted and equally adept,
they receive cups and pass the wine.
Toasts exchanged,
all follow ritual without fault.
Playing the zither and blowing the flute,
the melody lingers in the breeze.
Clear notes and mournful tunes,
move listeners to deeper sorrow.
Guests recite poems of drunken return,
the host says the dew is not yet dry.
Joyful feasts continue day and night,
ending with harmonious and graceful delight.
Thus, on the late spring purification festival,
the third day of the third month,
carriages traveled side by side,
for the cleansing rites by the sunny riverbank.
Vermilion canopies formed continuous nets,
shining across the fields and reflecting the clouds.
Men and women in splendid attire,
came and went in colorful profusion.
Adorned to the utmost, displaying allure,
graceful and charming.
With subtle glances and flowing looks,
their arched eyebrows like silkworms.
Then, young lads from Qí sang while maidens from Zhào stood in rows.
Seated, they sang southern songs; rising, they danced Zhèng dances.
White cranes seemed to fly, silkworms to spin their threads.
Long sleeves swirled and filled the courtyard,
silk stockings stepped lightly, lingering with ease.
Fluttering continuously as if about to cease,
dazzling, nearly falling only to rise again.
Lifting lightly, delaying,
limping and whirling.
They wove the deepened sorrows of autumn’s ninefold grief,
lamenting the winding tunes of western Jīng.
Zithers were plucked, panpipes blown,
renewing the melodies with fresh sounds.
Widows chanted mournfully,
pheasants cried in sorrow.
Those seated sighed in anguish,
their souls shaken, spirits wounded.
Then the assembled gentlemen set forth,
galloping across the sandy fields.
Fine steeds raced with bits aligned,
crossbows drawn with yellow triggers.
Feet swift as startling gusts,
arrowheads splitting the finest hairs.
Stooping, they pierced bream and chub;
looking up, they brought down pairs of wild geese.
Fish had no time to flee,
birds no leisure to soar.
Then they boarded light boats, floating on clear pools,
crisscrossing northern islets, reaching southern shores.
Waves splashed as the boats swayed gracefully,
the river god Yáng Hóu stirred the waters, covering ducks and gulls.
They pursued water leopards, lashed at river monsters,
awed by kuí dragons, terrified of flood dragons.
As the day approached dusk,
the revelers remained unrestrained.
Ending the joy, they summoned their carriages,
parting ways by the winding ponds.
Chariots thundered like wind-driven storms,
horses leapt like deer, arched like dragons.
At evening’s return,
their joy was unforgettable.
This is the pleasure of excursions and sightseeing,
delight for eyes and ears.
Those who have not witnessed its beauty
are hardly fit to praise it.
Now, Nányáng
is truly what is called the old capital of Hàn.
In ancient times, Empress Liú savored the dragon paste there,
and gazing toward Lǔ County, moved her residence.
Honoring the former emperor and continuing filial rites,
she established the Táng sacrifice at Yáo Mountain.
Thus the sacred root was fixed in Xià’s lineage,
flourishing only after three dynasties.
Without the grand design of pure virtue,
who could measure and dwell there!
In recent times, Marquis Kǎo longed for the past,
finding no peace in his dwelling.
Disdaining Chángshā’s lack of joy,
he journeyed north across the Jiāng and Xiāng rivers.
He shone with vermilion light at Báishuǐ,
and through nine generations achieved soaring glory.
Observing this region’s divine greatness,
he awakened to heaven’s will and inspired spirits.
As for its palaces and buildings,
there are gardens, huts, and old estates,
towering and lofty.
The imperial chambers are solemn yet magnificent,
connected pavilions gleaming in mutual splendor.
Here the sacred emperor roamed at ease,
and divine spirits found protection and peace.
Zhānglíng mound luxuriant with verdure,
the pure temple serene and subtle.
The imperial ancestors descend to enjoy offerings and bestow blessings,
for ten thousand sacrifices without decline.
Emperors and kings praised its exclusive beauty,
chanting southern airs as they turned their thoughts.
Moreover, its gentlemen
are broad-minded, wise, and discerning,
truly respectful, gentle, and kind.
Their demeanor is exemplary,
their speech elegant.
Advancing, retreating, bending, stretching,
they rise and fall with the times.
Now, as heaven and earth are in discord,
the emperor’s governance is disordered,
wolves and tigers run rampant,
it is the season for the true man to revolutionize the mandate.
Here then are strategists and martial generals,
all able to seize the fierce and subdue the violent,
shattering the hard and crushing the strong.
Forcing open barred gates,
trampling over Xiányáng.
Emperor Gāozǔ trod this path,
Emperor Guāngwǔ gathered its heroes.
Thus the passes were closed against invasion,
and Hàn’s virtue long endured.
And when they left danger for safety,
they considered the people in their migrations.
Men like Zhōu and Shào,
occupying the tripod’s legs,
managed the king’s duties.
The class of officials and gentry,
weaving through classics and instructions,
offered words for adoption.
Thus the court knew no flawed governance,
and its influence shone brightly.
Then the elderly with teeth like serrated fish,
the hunchbacked ancients,
white-haired and crowned with yellow locks,
sighed together and sang:
“We gaze at the kingfisher plumes, so luxuriant,
the grand standard erected, flowing gracefully.
Four flying dragons stride powerfully,
harmonious bells resound in the capital.
Gathering ten thousand chariots, they linger,
proceeding along level roads to return.”
How could they not long for the words of the Son of Heaven’s southern tour!
Thus a eulogy was composed:
The imperial ancestor settled here,
Emperor Guāngwǔ arose here.
Holding the Hé and Luò rivers,
he unified the four seas.
Root and branches for a hundred generations,
occupying the Son of Heaven’s position.
Eternally filial,
cherishing the mulberry and catalpa of home.
The true man tours south,
beholding his old village.
Now, the Shījīng has six principles,
the second of which is called fù.
Yáng Xióng said:
“The poet’s fù is beautiful yet principled.”
Bān Gù said:
“The fù
is a branch of ancient poetry.”
The ancient kings collected them
to observe local customs.
Seeing
“green bamboo, lush and graceful,”
they knew it was the produce of Qí’s banks in Wèi;
seeing
“in their plank houses,”
they knew it was the dwellings of the Western Róng in Qín’s wilds.
Thus they could distinguish all regions while seated.
Yet Sīmǎ Xiàngrú, in his fù “Shànglín,” cited
“black oranges ripen in summer,”
Yáng Xióng, in his fù “Gānquán,” described
“jade trees, verdant and lush,”
Bān Gù, in his fù “Xīdū,” marveled at the appearance of flatfish,
Zhāng Héng, in his fù “Xījīng,” narrated a journey to see the sea god Ruò.
They invented rare marvels
for embellishment.
Such things as these
are not limited to here.
Examining the fruit trees,
they grew not in their native soil;
checking the divine creatures,
they emerged not from their proper places.
In diction, they are easily adorned,
in meaning, empty and unsubstantiated.
Moreover, a jade cup without a bottom,
though precious, is useless;
extravagant words without proof,
though beautiful, lack canonical basis.
Yet critics never fail to condemn their refined essence,
and authors largely uphold them as models.
Habit becomes custom,
and this has long been so.
Having contemplated imitating the "Two Capitals" to compose the "Three Metropolises,"
their mountains, rivers, cities, and towns
I verified against maps;
their birds, beasts, plants, and trees
I examined through local records.
Folk songs, dances, and music
each adhere to their customs;
the stalwart and venerable elders
are all authentic to their origins.
Why is this?
Those who speak in verse
sing of their aspirations;
those who ascend heights and compose fu
praise what they behold.
To laud objects, one must value grounding them in their essence;
to extol events, one should base them on their reality.
If not grounded in essence or reality,
how can readers trust it?
Moreover, the principle of levying tribute according to local produce
is recorded in the Yú Shū;
distinguishing objects and situating them appropriately
is cautioned in the Zhōu Yì.
I shall briefly illustrate one aspect,
capture its essence,
and return to the realm of classical exegesis.
There was a young master from Western Shǔ
who spoke to a princely scion of Eastern Wú,
saying:
"I have heard that heaven takes the sun and moon as its guiding principles,
and earth takes the four seas as its order.
The nine regions are divided like stars,
and myriad states stand in disarray.
Xiáohán possesses the abode of emperors,
while Héluò is the dwelling of kings.
Have you, sir, perhaps also heard of the affairs of Shǔ's capital?
Allow me to outline and present them to you.
"Now, Shǔ's capital
had its foundations laid in antiquity,
and its state was established in the middle ages.
It expanded Língguān to serve as its gate,
encompassed Yùlěi to form its domain.
Girded by the twin flows of the two rivers,
it confronts the formidable barriers of Éméi.
Where water and land converge,
it unites the six directions in intersection;
where lush abundance thrives,
it flourishes across the eight regions in verdant profusion.
"To the front, it strides across Qiánzāng,
and rests against Jiāozhǐ.
The routes that traverse it
extend over five thousand lǐ.
Mountains and hills connect continuously,
embracing streams and cradling valleys.
Ridges and peaks intertwine chaotically,
touching stones to exhale clouds.
Lush and verdant in emerald hues,
towering and majestic in lofty grandeur.
Piercing the azure heavens with elegant prominence,
unfurling crimson mists to form rosy clouds.
Lóngchí's waterfall gushes fiercely at its bends,
Lòujiāng's subterranean flow bursts forth at its slopes.
Turbulent as Tānggǔ's surging waves,
torrential as Méngsì's swelling billows.
Here, Qióng bamboo fringes the ridges,
Dragon eye trees flourish alongside,
litchi trees grow laterally.
Spreading lush, luxuriant green leaves,
bearing bright, scattered red fruits.
They greet deep winter without withering,
ever radiant and graceful.
Peacocks and kingfishers flock in flight,
rhinoceroses and elephants race in gallop.
White pheasants crow at dawn,
gibbons wail at night.
The golden horse gallops with gleaming light, leaving no trace behind,
the azure chicken flashes suddenly, displaying its splendor.
Fire wells sink their glow into deep springs,
high flames soar and blaze at the sky's edge.
Among them lie amber and cinnabar,
river pearls and flawless gems.
Gold sands and silver gravel,
their patterns brilliantly vivid,
resplendent and dazzling.
"To the rear, it turns its back to Huáróng,
pointing north toward Kūnlún.
Bordered by Jiàngé,
barricaded by Shímén.
The flowing Hàn River surges mightily,
its startling waves thunderously rush.
Gazing from afar, the heavens seem to revolve;
approaching near, the clouds appear dim.
Aquatic creatures vary in kind,
scaly and shelled beings differ in clan.
Some conceal flood dragons,
others hide jasper jade.
Fine fish emerge from Bǐngxué,
excellent timber clusters in Bāogǔ.
Among its trees are magnolia, cassia,
sophora, catalpa, paulownia,
palm, areca, maple, and fir.
Nánmu and cedar flourish densely in valley depths,
pine and cypress grow lushly on mountain peaks.
They raise tall trunks,
erect lengthy boughs.
They fan flying clouds,
brush against the light sky.
Xīhé borrows passage through steep forks,
the sunbird turns its wings at lofty summits.
Nesting and perching in flight,
they even surpass Dènglín.
Cave-dwelling strange beasts,
nest-roosting exotic birds.
Bears and brown bears roar on its sunny side,
eagles and ospreys swoop on its shaded side.
Gibbons and apes leap through sparse spaces, competing in agility,
tigers and leopards roar long and sing endlessly.
"To the east lies left-bank Mián and Bāzhōng,
filled with the Bǎipú tribes.
Externally, it bears the Copper Ridge at Dàngqú;
internally, it contains crucial strongholds within fertile lands.
Among these are Bā beans and Bā medicinals,
longevity bamboos and peach-branch bamboos.
Fenced by zǔ-plant gardens,
bordered by salt ponds.
Lizards dwell on mountains,
softshell turtles and tortoises inhabit waters.
Hidden dragons coil in marshy wetlands,
responding to drumbeats to summon rain.
Cinnabar glows crimson on its slopes,
honeycombs bloom luxuriantly over its mounds.
Shāntú gathered herbs and attained the Way,
Chìfǔ ingested them and achieved immortality.
As for the fierce and bold born in this region,
their ballads exalt martial prowess.
Roused, they form the Cóng militia;
at play, they perform the Yú dance.
Their sharp spirit shone in the middle era,
their vigorous posture endured in the Music Bureau.
"To the west, it embraces the Mín Mountains on the right,
where surging streams and rivers arise.
Accompanied by the Báiláng tribe,
their folk songs form elegant verses.
The wilderness is vast and untamed,
the forests and foothills dark and deep.
Here grow the jiāoràng trees,
where squatting owls hide.
A hundred medicinal herbs flourish in thickets,
cold blossoms fragrant even in winter.
Diverse species abound in multitude,
what does not thrive here?
Among them are green pearls and yellow huán,
green nú stones and mángxiāo.
Some are rich with green tí plants,
some lush with red peppers.
Míwú herbs spread across the central slopes,
fēnglián vines creep over orchid-covered banks.
Red blossoms with purple adornments,
branches and leaves gradually unfurl.
Flowers bloom luxuriantly,
falling petals drift and flutter.
Shénnóng once tasted them,
Lú and Fū prepared them.
Their fragrance dispels evil qi,
their flavors cleanse ailments and fevers.
Within its borders,
there are plains, marshes, mounds, and lowlands,
stretching far and wide in view.
Nourished by the Qián and Mò rivers,
irrigated by the Mián and Luò streams.
Ditches and channels spread like veins,
fields and boundaries interlace like brocade.
Millet and sorghum grow lush,
rice and paddy thrive abundantly.
Pointing to the canal's mouth as the Cloud Gate,
sprinkling the Biāo Pond to create land marshes.
Even the pouring rain of the constellation Bì,
cannot match its nourishing moisture.
Then the settlements are densely prosperous,
nestled between rivers and mountains.
Roofs and houses face each other,
mulberry and catalpa trees connect continuously.
Each home has a salt spring well,
each household a garden of oranges and pomelos.
In their orchards grow pomegranates and loquats,
oranges, persimmons, yǐng, and tíng.
Hairy peaches stand in rows,
plums and prunes spread out.
A hundred fruits burst from their husks,
different colors share the same glory.
Red cherries ripen in spring,
white pears mature in summer.
Then when the Great Fire star flows,
cool winds grow fierce.
White dew condenses,
light frost forms.
Purple pears become moist and glossy,
zhēn chestnuts split open.
Grapes burst randomly, pomegranates compete to crack.
Sweetness reaches its peak and falls naturally,
fragrance intense and overpowering.
Their gardens have jǔruò and zhūyú,
melon fields and taro patches.
Sugarcane and spicy ginger,
bask in sun or thrive in shade.
Day by day they flourish subtly,
month by month they spread luxuriantly.
According to the land's bounty,
all offerings are stored.
In its fertile marshes grow clustered jiǎng and thick cattails,
green water chestnuts and red lotuses.
Mixed with wěn algae,
blended with duckweed and fán.
Stems clustered densely,
leaves wrapped luxuriantly.
When fruits ripen in season,
lords and princes feast on them.
Among them are companions of swans and cranes,
zhèn herons, egrets, and pelicans.
Morning wild ducks arrive at dawn,
migratory geese carry reeds.
When leaves fall, they fly south,
when ice melts, they journey north.
Soaring through clouds, resting on water,
singing clearly in pure streams.
In the depths dwell white soft-shelled turtles and commanding turtles,
black otters offer sacrifices upstream.
Zhān, wěi, zūn, and fáng fish,
tí, lǐ, shā, and cháng fish.
Scales arranged in order, colors varied,
brocade-like patterns and intricate markings.
Leaping in waves, playing in rapids,
in midstream they forget each other.
"Thus, walls of metal and ramparts of stone,
encircle the central region.
Both splendid and lofty,
truly named Chéngdū.
Opening eighteen grand gates,
marking wide roads for parallel carriages.
Building new palaces on high, dry ground,
modeling after Chéngmíng and erecting halls.
Connecting Yángchéng's extended galleries,
with soaring towers and pavilions in the clouds.
Opening tall verandas facing mountains,
lining elegant windows overlooking rivers.
Inside are council halls and noble chambers,
Wǔyì and Hǔwēi halls.
Gates of Xuānhuà,
portals of Chónglǐ.
Magnificent twin towers stand distant,
layered gates open wide.
Golden knockers reflect each other,
jade lintels shine mutually.
Outside, tracks extend in eight directions,
neighborhood gates face each other.
Houses adjoin, roofs connect,
thousands of corridors, myriad rooms.
There are also elite mansions,
facing streets and avenues.
Platforms and courtyards grand and spacious,
high gates admitting four-horse carriages.
Courtyards resonate with bells and chimes,
halls echo with zithers and lutes.
If not for Gé or Jiāng,
who could care for this?
"Adjacent is the Shǎochéng,
connecting to its west.
Where markets converge,
a deep pool of ten thousand merchants.
Rows of streets a hundred layers deep,
thousands of shops arrayed.
Goods and wealth pile like mountains,
fine fabrics shine like stars.
Capital gentlemen and ladies,
in splendid attire and elegant makeup.
Merchants trade and sell,
crisscrossing in all directions.
Exotic goods rise wondrously,
surpassing all eight regions.
Cloth includes tónghuā fabric,
flour from guāngláng trees.
Qióng canes pass through Dàxià cities,
jǔ sauce spreads its flavor to Pānyū lands.
Carriages and palanquins mingle chaotically,
caps and sashes blend together.
Wheels accumulate, tracks overlap,
sprawling and leaning against each other.
Noise boils like a cauldron,
clamor fills the universe;
dust and din reach the sky,
haze dims the shining sun.
Within market walls,
homes of skilled artisans.
A hundred workshops separate rooms,
looms harmonize together.
Embroidered shell-pattern brocade finely made,
washed in river waves for color.
Huángrùn cloth compared to bamboo tubes,
carried in baskets of gold.
Extravagant and immensely wealthy,
rivaling the fame of Zhuó and Zhèng.
Lords monopolize mountains and rivers,
trade thrives in private courtyards.
Hoarded coins number in the millions,
pi and guī coins presented together.
Also powerful through wealth,
flourishing in border cities.
The magnates of Sānshǔ,
come and go with the times.
Cultivating connections in the capital,
forming cliques and attaching to factions.
Engaging in intense debates and playful discussions,
gripping wrists and clapping hands.
Going out with linked riders,
returning with a hundred carriages.
As for their old customs,
from winter's end to spring's start.
On auspicious days and fine hours,
they set wine in high halls,
to entertain honored guests.
Golden léi vessels placed in the center,
dishes and fruits arrayed on four sides.
Toasting with clear piǎo wine,
savoring fresh purple-scaled fish.
Feather-tipped cups raised in competition,
strings and bamboo instruments then play.
Bā maidens pluck strings,
Hàn women beat rhythm.
Raising western tunes from tight strings,
singing songs of the river's swiftness.
Swinging long sleeves in repeated dance,
gracefully fluttering and gliding.
Sharing cups, drawing seats close,
filling cups to the brim, penalizing each other.
Reveling in drink tonight,
drunk for months on end.
"As for the likes of the princely scions,
the peers of Xìgōng.
Chasing game in the wilds,
the lanes are left without residents.
All ride fine steeds,
clad in fish-scale patterns.
Dark and yellow banners differ in their ranks,
teams of four horses interweave in splendor.
Westward they cross the Golden Dike,
eastward they pass the Jade Ford.
From the new moon they part until the month's end,
not a day, not a ten-day period.
Treading through dense undergrowth,
traversing vast and open wilderness.
Hawks and hounds swiftly dart,
nets and snares spread like curtains.
Furred creatures scatter in disarray,
feathered flocks descend in chaos.
With sudden sounds and swift movements,
they are caught in nets amidst the woods.
They slaughter muntjacs and elk,
cut down yaks and deer.
Adorned with patterned serpents,
astride carved tigers.
Ambitions not yet fulfilled,
the day draws to a close.
Pursuing swift wings,
venturing to the farthest reaches.
Exiting the gates of Péngmén,
galloping down the Nine-Bend Slope.
Traversing the towering Three Gorges,
treading the rugged paths of the Five Peaks.
Spearing iron-eating beasts,
shooting venom-biting deer.
Startling the tiger-people in the grassy plains,
shooting talking birds in the dense forests.
Pulling out elephant tusks,
breaking off rhinoceros horns.
Birds with broken wings,
beasts with crippled legs.
"Exhausted, they return,
together ranking like Diānchí,
gathering at the river isles.
Testing the water travelers,
mooring light boats.
Wooing the river goddesses,
roaming with the spirits.
Catching kingfishers,
fishing for catfish and bream.
Bringing down high-flying swans,
drawing out hidden dragons.
Blowing the dòngxiāo flute,
singing rowing songs.
Stirring the sturgeon fish,
moving the Yánghóu deity.
Waves surge and boil,
pearls and shells float and drift.
Like the Milky Way holding stars,
its radiance illuminates the vast flow.
Those about to feast on the hunt,
spread canopies and tents,
meet on the open plains.
Pour clear wine,
slice fragrant delicacies.
Drinking and feasting to intoxication,
guests and companions depart.
Carriages and horses thunder like awe,
rumbling and clamoring.
Like wind scattering rain,
spreading across hundreds of miles.
This is the peace and joy of dwelling in this land,
the excitement seen and heard.
How can only the Three Rivers
be the world's court and market?
"As for the extraordinary and marvelous,
unrestrained and endless.
One thread of divine wonders,
one weave of human principles.
Distant, the essence of Mínshān,
above forms the well-constellation.
The Heavenly Emperor determines the cycle and brings prosperity,
blessings descend and flourish.
Green jade emerges from Chánghóng's blood,
birds are born from Dùyǔ's spirit.
Wild transformations beyond the ordinary,
praised as magnificent since ancient times.
Nearby, the Jiānghàn rivers shine with spirit,
each generation bears its heroes.
Brilliant like Xiàngrú,
pure like Jūnpíng.
Wáng Bāo, resplendent and outstanding,
Yáng Xióng, endowed with talent and born distinguished.
Profound thoughts adorned with virtue,
literary brilliance displayed before the heavenly court.
Examined across the four seas as outstanding,
renowned in the middle era.
Thus, travelers and talkers praise them,
creators take them as models.
As for fortresses at the valleys,
barriers relying on mountains.
Steep ridges form long walls like the Great Wall,
narrow passes swallow like great defenses.
One man guards the pass,
ten thousand cannot advance.
Gōngsūn leaped on his horse and declared himself emperor,
Liú Zōng descended from his carriage and proclaimed himself king.
From this perspective,
what in the world surpasses it?
Thus, even with the combined wealth of all Xià,
it still cannot match the boundlessness of this capital."
The Eastern Wú princely scion chuckled and laughed,
saying:
"Those who observe celestial signs above,
discern the patterns of heaven.
Those who assess the land and its products below,
analyze the principles of earth.
In ancient times and past dynasties,
they once surveyed the grand legacy of the eight directions.
Unifying the six directions and glorifying their dwellings,
soaring and gathering in distant realms.
Bird-track scripts on silk,
jade tablets and stone records.
Where have they heard of Liáng and Mín having imperial inspection lodges
or the foundations of traveling palaces?
Yet you speak of Shǔ's wealth,
the possessions of Yútóng.
Extolling its regions,
praising its forests and marshes.
Boasting of the barriers of Bā and Hàn,
considering them the pinnacle of strategic defense.
Following the fertility of the squatting owl,
believing it saves the world from calamities.
Petty and narrow-minded,
indeed also lamented by the parochial.
Rambling and discussing capitals,
hardly the grand spectacle of great men.
Why so?
The soil is insufficient to sustain life,
the mountains and rivers inadequate for full defense.
Gōngsūn established a state there and was destroyed,
Zhūgě made it his home and perished.
This is the ruin of chaos and disorder,
the track of overthrow and collapse.
How can it compare to the kings and lords and display majestic achievements?
Playing with its gravel without glimpsing the jade abyss,
one knows not where the black dragon coils.
Accustomed to its wretched town without seeing the superior state,
one knows not where the heroes tread.
"Have you alone not heard of the great magnificence of Wú?
Moreover, the founding of Wú,
began with Tàibó,
proclaimed by Yánlíng.
It is where upright governance was manifested,
where lofty principles arose.
Establishing supreme virtue to create an enterprise,
an era unmatched and gloriously praised.
Through humility and yielding, customs were established,
lightly discarding a thousand chariots.
If discussing capitals across the land,
it is not what other states hope to rival.
Thus, in its strategic planning,
it aligns with the stellar divisions above.
Expanding territory and drawing borders,
outstandingly annexing and merging.
Encompassing Gānyuè,
straddling and stepping over Mánjīng.
The Wùnǚ constellation lends its radiance,
the Yìzhěn constellations harbor its essence.
Pointing to Héngyuè to stabilize the wilds,
gazing at Lóngchuān to gird the outskirts.
"As for its mountains and marshes,
they are lofty, precipitous, towering, and rugged,
dark, deep, dense, and steep.
The waters gush and surge,
vast and boundless.
Some burst forth to open channels,
others swallow rivers and take in the Hàn.
Piled high and heaped up,
rushing and flowing.
They stretch across several provinces,
irrigating half the world.
A hundred streams branch out,
converging as they return to the sea.
Controlling the clear and drawing the turbid,
mingling waves and rapids.
Surging and boiling,
silent and far-flowing.
Roaring with great force,
rumbling with hidden power.
Emerging from the midst of the great wilderness,
flowing beyond the eastern extremity.
Passing through the forests of Fúsāng,
encompassing the vastness of Tānggǔ.
Tidal waves rise tumultuously,
swirling back for ten thousand lǐ.
Mist billows densely,
clouds steam and darken.
Deep, clear, and swirling,
vast, expansive, and shimmering.
Its depth cannot be fathomed,
its breadth cannot be measured.
Vast and tranquil without shore,
gathering all flows to become long.
Here gather and breed wondrous creatures,
scaled and armored beings congregate.
"Here, long whales swallow ships,
giant salamanders spew waves.
Leaping dragons and soaring serpents,
jiāo, zī, pí, and pá fish.
Kingly wěi, hóu, and tái fish,
yìn turtles and fānzé fish.
Cuttlefish and sword-bearing crabs,
qū bì, qīng, and è creatures,
swim and dive within.
With scaled armor finely adorned,
strange kinds intermingle.
Against and with the current,
gasping and floating.
Among birds are kūn chickens, zhú, and yù birds,
shuāng cranes, egrets, and wild geese.
Yuánjū birds avoid the wind,
migratory geese arrive at the river.
Xīchì and yónglú birds,
jīng cranes, qiū, and cāng birds.
Storks, gulls, yì, and lú birds,
float freely above.
Their feathers glisten,
following the waves in uneven array.
Preening wings and arranging plumes,
leisurely amusing themselves.
Pecking at trailing algae,
brushing through rippling waves.
Fish and birds clamor,
all creatures teem with life.
Vast and dim,
bewildering and sudden,
divine transformations swift and sudden,
containing darkness and nurturing light.
Exhausting nature and form,
fullness and emptiness follow nature.
Clams and pearl-bearing oysters,
wax and wane with the moon.
Giant turtles bearing mountains,
their heads crowned with sacred peaks.
The great péng bird flutters,
wings like hanging heavens.
Stirring the vast currents,
thunderously clapping in deep abysses.
Shaking the cosmos,
how can its origin be fully told!
"Islands stretch far and wide,
islets rise high.
Gazing afar into the distance,
looking out into dim obscurity.
Rare wonders are splendid,
strange gaps are filled.
Paths are cut off,
yet wind and clouds connect.
Grand peach trees twist and coil,
crimson cassias form thickets.
Jade-like branches raise stems and spread blossoms,
coral grows dense and exquisite.
Added ridges and layered barriers,
dwellings of perfected beings.
Jade halls face eaves,
stone chambers stand opposite.
Lush green canopies,
graceful plain-clad maidens.
Jiāng Féi comes and goes here,
Hǎi Tóng feasts and converses here.
This is truly a divine and marvelous scene,
alas, difficult to describe in detail!
"Then the land's configuration is uneven,
plants and trees spread and creep.
Where marshes are encountered, they become gardens;
where forests are met, they become parks.
Unusual flowers, lush and flourishing,
blooming in summer, verdant in winter.
Distinguished in local records,
envied by the central plains.
Among herbs are huò, nà, cardamom,
ginger, and various kinds.
Such as jiānglí,
and types of seaweed.
Silk ribbons, purple and deep red,
edible kudzu, fragrant grasses.
Stone sails and water pines,
dōngfēng and fúliú plants.
Spread over marshlands,
extending over hills and mounds.
Clinging to mountain peaks,
covering rivers and seas.
Shaking white stems,
bearing red blossoms.
Lush and luxuriant,
brilliant and fragrant.
Colors dazzling and bright,
scents pervasive and strong.
Tribute presents them in bundled packages,
the 'Lísāo' sings of their enduring growth.
Among trees are maple, xiá, camphor,
palm, gǒu, and láng trees.
Mián, yuán, chūn, and lú trees,
patterned xiāng, zhēn, and jiāng trees.
Píngzhòng and jūnqiān trees,
pine, zǐ, and gǔdù trees.
Nánliú trees,
longing trees.
Clustered on high ridges,
flourishing in secluded hills.
Trunks soar a thousand xún,
shade spreads over ten thousand mǔ.
Branches cluster, stems intertwine,
layered blossoms, overlapping leaves.
Gnarled and coiled like dragons,
scales densely joined.
Glorious colors blend,
intricate like rich embroidery.
Night dew dense and heavy,
morning sun dim and hazy.
Swaying with the wind,
rustling and whistling.
Branches sing in harmonious rhythm,
flying sounds clear and bright.
Like zithers and zhù instruments playing together,
shēng and yú pipes singing in unison.
Above them, father monkeys mournfully chant,
young ones longly cry.
Yòu, wú, and guǒrán creatures,
leap, jump, fly, and bound.
Vying to hang suspended,
competing to roam distant branches.
Startled, scurrying in chaos,
scattered, fleeing in disarray.
Below them are xiāo yáng, qí wolves,
yàyǔ, chū, and elephants.
Tribes of wū and tú,
gangs of rhinoceros and sì.
Hooks for claws, saws for teeth,
naturally forming sharp points.
Gleaming like shining stars,
roaring like crashing thunder.
Names recorded in the 'Shānhāi Jīng',
forms engraved on the Xià dynasty ding."
"The bamboos here are the yúndāng and línyū,
the guìjiàn and shètǒng.
The yòuwú has its groves,
the piǎoláo grows in clusters.
Their shoots sprout joints,
often twining and intertwining.
Green leaves and emerald stems
brave frost and halt snow.
Tall and dense they stand,
lush and rustling.
Graceful and elegant,
jade-smooth and jade-fresh.
Even the cloud-touching tips cannot surpass them,
nor can the valley of Xiègǔ match them.
The yuèzhuó feeds on their fruit,
the yuānchú frolics among them.
The fruits here include red tangerines and yúgān,
forests of lìzhī.
The bīngláng has no branches,
the coconut leaves offer no shade.
Lóngyǎn and gǎnlǎn,
chánliú that withstands frost.
Their roots take hold in the shade of Bǐjǐng,
their trunks stand in the sun of Héngshān.
Their white blossoms are splendid,
their red blooms fragrant.
They face green cliffs,
and hang with purple fruits.
The zhègū flies south yet lingers here,
the peacock displays its plumage and soars.
The pheasant returns flying to roost,
the kingfisher nests in rows.
The treasures here are from the hills of kūnyáo,
the borders of copper and iron.
The fire-aligned gems,
the treasures that startle chickens.
Crimson cinnabar and bright pearls,
golden flowers and silver ore.
Purple shells and flowing sulfur,
pale green jade and plain jade.
Hidden and abundant, towering and rugged,
mixed and inserted in secluded screens.
Their essence shines, hidden yet sprouting,
piled and fallen in mountain valleys.
The rocky shores do not wither because of them,
the forests are moistened and enriched by them.
The Marquis of Suí would disdain his night-shining pearl,
the King of Sòng would belittle his jiélù gem.
"As for the remote and strange corners,
there are dragon caves steaming within,
storing clouds and rain.
The línglǐ resembles a beast,
floating stones resemble rafts.
Paired are the bǐmù fish,
single are the wángyú fish.
On land, they drink from trees,
in deep waters, they dwell.
The spring chamber weaves hidden silk and rolls fine gauze,
the abyss dweller weeps pearls in sorrow.
Open the north door to face the sun,
align the southern sea with the dark capital.
Across the four wilds, field paths are countless,
fertile lands doubled in abundance.
Plains and marshes differ in kind,
lowlands and highlands vary in grade.
Elephants plow and birds weed,
this happens naturally here.
Fine grains and wild rice ears,
are found here.
Boil seawater to make salt,
mine mountains to cast coins.
The state taxes twice-ripened rice,
the villages tribute silk from eight broods of silkworms.
"Observe the inner depths of its suburbs,
the order of its capital city.
The foundation of hegemon kings,
the base of founding a state.
Outer walls encircle all around,
double city walls meet at corners.
Sixteen gates in total,
waterways and land roads.
Thus it was planned and begun,
to last a thousand generations.
Modeled after the Purple Palace to build its halls,
expanding the vast courtyard endlessly.
Cold and heat are kept out by deep chambers,
rainbows encircle the cloud-like pavilions.
Thus it stands majestic, brilliant for ten thousand miles.
They built the high terrace of Gūsū,
overlooking the four distances, uniquely erected.
Girded by the deep pools of morning and evening,
adorned with the lush gardens of Chángzhōu.
Peek into the treasury of Dōngshān,
and rare treasures fill the eyes; glimpse
the granaries of Hǎilíng,
and red grains overflow.
They erected ancestral temples in Wǔchāng,
made detached palaces in Jiànyè.
Expanding what Hé Lǘ once built,
adopting the methods left by Fūchāi.
Raise the glorious halls of the divine dragon,
set ornate railings in jagged rows.
Exalt the towering heights of Línhǎi,
adorn the brilliance of Chìwū.
East and west interwoven,
north and south lofty.
Rooms and windows face each other,
connecting pavilions in series.
Gates and doors ingeniously designed,
uniquely named with odd titles.
The left called Wānqí,
the right named Línxíng.
Carved rafters and engraved brackets,
green-patterned doors and red pillars.
Painted with cloud patterns,
depicted with immortal spirits.
Though this dwelling is extravagant and beautiful,
it is still not enough to bring slight peace.
Aspiring to match every house with tilted palaces,
all built with jade and constructed with jasper.
High gates stand imposing,
wide doorways fit two carriages side by side.
Vermilion towers stand in pairs,
imperial roads smooth as whetstone.
Planted with green locust trees,
spanned by clear waters.
Dark shades loom deep,
clear streams flow steadily.
Official buildings line for seven miles,
flanking the sunny road.
Garrison camps close like comb teeth,
government offices scattered like chess pieces.
Héngtáng and Cháxià,
village houses grand and boastful.
Chánggān stretches continuously,
flying eaves interlock.
"Its residents are of noble gates and great wealth,
towering and heroic figures.
Descendants of Yú and Wèi,
offspring of Gù and Lù.
Wise and gifted, inheriting legacies,
mature and experienced for generations.
Galloping horses leave overlapping tracks,
red-wheeled carriages leave repeated ruts.
They return with weapons arrayed,
spears and racks set within.
Official caps and canopies shade like clouds,
streets and alleys bustling and crowded.
Their neighbors include the dashing knights,
the swift and daring guests.
Forming friendships with grace,
attendants numerous and splendid.
They step out in pearl-studded shoes,
moving in hundreds and thousands.
Feasting in neighborhoods, drinking in lanes,
raising cups and toasting with white jade.
Lifting gates and hoisting tripods,
competing in archery, pitch-pot, and gambling.
Póyáng-style wild revelry,
fueled by wine and stirred to action.
"Thus joy is abundant and feasting never lacking,
the capital prospers and the four corners come.
By water they float, by land they travel,
double boats and four-horse carriages.
Singing rowers and turning wheels,
from dawn till dusk.
Markets open early and accept all,
shops overflow across streets.
Mixing all goods in the same market,
uniting capital and outskirts as one.
Men and women gaze in wonder,
merchants crowd shoulder to shoulder.
Hemp clothes and fine linen garments,
mingling and gathering in throngs.
Light carriages rein in through tunnels,
tall ships raise sails past shops.
Fruits and cloth converge as usual,
distant treasures like liúlí and kēdá.
Wealth and goods in chaos,
utensils of myriad kinds.
Gold ingots piled high,
pearl strings spread out.
Peach-bark mats and ivory mats,
stored in bamboo tubes;
banana cloth and fine silk,
softer than gauze and plain silk.
Chatter and clamor,
trading and competing.
Noise and uproar,
fragrant and dazzling.
Sleeves waved like wind,
red dust darkens the day.
Sweat pours like drizzle,
and the main roads turn muddy.
"Among the wealthy commoners,
are those skilled in trade.
Seizing opportunities to pursue profit,
their riches swell to immense fortunes.
Competing for territory,
they annex fields and lanes;
boasting of their leisurely lives,
they wear pearl-adorned garments and feast on jade-like delicacies.
The agile and fierce,
dwell side by side here.
Swift as Qìngjì,
brave as Zhuānzhū.
They don tall caps when venturing out,
stride forth with swords held high.
Adorned with shark-skin scabbards,
they wield blades like Shǔlòu.
Concealing spears among the people,
they depart from the alleys, leaving behind their fierce dogs.
Each household has crane-knee bows,
each door boasts rhinoceros-hide shields.
Military readiness is stored for use,
weapons and equipment amply stocked.
Wú hooks and Yuè halberds,
Chúnjūn and Zhànlú swords.
War chariots fill Shíchéng,
spear boats blanket the rivers and lakes.
"Dew gives way to frost,
sun and moon pass by.
Plants shed their leaves,
birds and beasts grow plump.
Observing hawks and falcons,
warning the conscripted men.
Seated in linked armor,
raising the Sìgū banners.
Commanding officers to grasp their bells,
leading the grand hunt at Jùqū.
The Wūhǔ and Lánghuǎng,
the Fūnán and Xītú.
Chiefs of Dān'ěr and Hēichǐ,
leaders of Jīnlíng and Xiàngjùn.
Swift as galloping steeds,
nimble and alert,
they scout the path ahead.
Mounted scouts gallop along the roads,
compasses guide the direction.
Chariots rumble forth,
armored troops clang with each step.
The King of Wú then dons his jade-adorned carriage,
yokes his Sùshuāng steeds.
Banner tassels like fish whiskers,
streamers shimmer with layered light.
Gripping the Wūhào bow,
wearing the Gānjiàng sword.
Feather pennants flutter,
mighty halberds gleam.
Shell helmets and ivory-tipped arrows,
woven patterns and bird insignia.
The six armies in uniform attire,
four steeds prance like dragons.
Steep traps set all around,
nets and snares spread everywhere.
Fine-meshed nets intricately knotted,
traps and pitfalls linked by ropes.
Enclosed by the Jiǔyí Mountains,
defended by the Yuán and Xiāng Rivers.
Light carriages in bustling disarray,
archers on horseback radiantly splendid.
Bare-chested warriors grappling hand-to-hand,
troops skilled in leaping and hurling stones.
With ape-like arms and fused ribs,
wildly leaping, fierce and untamed.
Eyes sharp as eagles and ospreys,
darting swiftly, soaring and swooping.
Now separating, now converging,
they leap and bound across the wild plains.
Troops with shields, spears, and lances,
bearing Yángyí and Bólú weapons.
Long spears and short blades,
charging forth with hair flowing free.
Agile and swift, advancing together,
silent with gag bits in their mouths.
Fluttering banners and pennants,
drifting across the dim, distant fields.
Drums and gongs echo through the mountains,
fires blaze through the forests.
Flames soar, smoke floats,
veiled in mist and shadow.
Roaring like thunder, crashing loudly,
peaks crumble, ridges collapse.
Birds flee heedless of shelter,
beasts run ignoring their cries.
Fierce tigers and leopards,
elk and deer.
Chasing six-hued steeds,
pursuing flying creatures.
Shooting down luan birds and wild swans,
targeting nimble macaques.
White pheasants fall,
black pheasants scatter.
Scaling sheer cliffs and jagged peaks,
traversing perilous heights.
Leaping over bamboo and cypress,
scrambling through wolfberry and nanmu.
The great boar bellows,
the divine dragon is subdued.
Hard arrowheads grow slick,
frosty blades stained with blood.
"Then, reining in the steeds, halting the carriage,
aligning bridles, pausing the procession.
Wandering and lingering,
gazing upon the lush, serene greenery.
Observing the commanders' valor,
and the soldiers' rising and falling spirits.
Feathered creatures use beaks and claws as blades,
furred beasts employ teeth and horns as spears,
all embodying their nature, responding swiftly to threats.
Thus, they are hooked and torn, becoming wounded,
charged and trampled, bones and sinews severed.
None escape blunted sharpness, dimmed gleam,
broken and crushed, utterly destroyed.
Even if there were stone forests of jagged peaks,
they would bare their arms and level them;
even if there were nine-headed mighty serpents,
they would lift their feet and trample them.
Overturning nest dwellings,
smashing open den abodes.
Reaching up to seize Jùnyí birds,
stomping down on jackals and tapirs.
Raiding the lairs of bears and brown bears,
plundering the dens of tigers and leopards.
Gibbons wail as they are captured,
macaques laugh as they are struck down.
Slaughtering the Bā snake,
extracting the elephant's skeleton.
Chopping off the roc's wings,
covering the vast marshes.
Nimble birds and cunning beasts,
dart about in hesitation.
Stumbling in the vast net,
forgetting how to glare fiercely,
losing their sense of advance or retreat.
Souls terrified, courage drained, tripping over themselves,
struck by arrows that pierce deep,
bodies toppling, shadows rigid.
Piling up, growing in number,
layered in chaotic heaps.
Emptying thickets and groves,
toppling ridges and peaks.
Caves devoid of boars and piglets,
thickets without deer or quails.
Wishing to borrow the path of Fēnglóng,
parting the lofty heavens to hunt on high.
Caging the sun and moon's crow and hare,
exhausting the perches and nests of all that flies or runs.
"The ravines are silent and still,
the ridges and hills are barren.
Fishing nets are full,
the catch is abundant.
Turning the chariot and gazing askance,
watching fish in the three rivers.
Sailing boats upon Pénglí Lake,
myriad vessels converge as one.
Great ships link stern to bow,
massive masts connect prow to stern.
Flying clouds cover the sea,
a sight beyond ordinary measure.
Layered towers stand like islands,
resembling Fāng Hú in the mist.
Surpassing the yìshǒu in elegance,
outshining the yúhuáng of old.
Silk curtains spread,
tassels woven.
Open the windows and shades,
mirror the water's expanse.
Oarsmen and helmsmen,
chosen from Mǐnyú.
Skilled at riding the long winds,
familiar with the spirit of the waves.
Valuing a thousand miles in an inch of time,
briefly ahead of schedule, just a moment.
Rowing songs sung,
flutes and pipes sound.
The great flow echoes,
shorebirds startle.
Archery released,
checking for snipe and wild geese.
The hunter's mechanism springs,
capturing the jiāojīng.
Hooks and bait crisscross,
nets and traps connect in succession.
Skill surpassing Zhān Gōng,
craft outdoing Rén Fù.
Trapping gudgeon and giant salamander,
catching eel, catfish, and shark.
Covering two flatfish,
netting shrimp and prawn.
Riding horseshoe crabs, turtles, and alligators,
sharing nets and snares alike.
Submerged tigers and hidden deer,
bound and restrained in confusion.
Sturgeon and whale caught among the baited hooks,
comets suddenly appear and connect.
Though one may fish for carp by the river,
it is no different from shooting a minnow in a well valley.
"Light boats gather and race,
meeting the tide and shaking the lines.
Imagining the reappearance of the píngshí fruit,
visiting the spirit kuí among the jiāo people.
Jīngwèi carrying stones meets the snare,
wényáo flying at night touches the line.
The northern mountains lose their soaring wings,
the western seas lose their swimming scales.
The tattooed-face men,
the carved-body soldiers.
Adorned like coiling dragons,
facing jiāo and chī.
Examining their splendid forms,
then lavish and extravagant brocade.
Assessing their fierce courage,
then fierce and wolf-like ferocity.
Together they explore hidden dangers,
search for rare wonders.
Feel the hawksbill turtle,
touch the giant clam.
Split giant clams in the deep abyss,
wash the bright moon in ripples.
"Exhausting the world's utmost wonders,
leaving nothing unsought, nothing unattained.
Streams and valleys emptied for this,
rivers and waterways left impoverished.
Smiling at Dāntái's schemes,
briefly raiding the sea for treasures.
Carrying Hàn women on the rear boats,
pursuing Jìn merchants amid the dust.
Surging with the current, crashing and rolling,
aided by the swift wind, whistling and howling.
Charging straight through waves up the rapids,
always surging and drifting endlessly.
Almost ready to rest and return victorious,
bowing to Tiān Wú and Yáng Hóu.
Pointing to Bāo Shān as the rendezvous,
gathering at Dòngtíng and lingering there.
Counting military spoils in the Guìlín gardens,
feasting the troops at Luòxīng Tower.
Setting out wine like the Huái and Sì rivers,
piling delicacies like hills and mountains.
Flying light carriages to pour green líng wine,
side by side with paired reins, offering rare delicacies.
Drinking beacons rise,
toasting drums thunder.
Soldiers shed weariness,
the crowd brims with joy.
Fortunate in the Guǎnwá Palace,
displaying female musicians to entertain the ministers.
Arraying metal, stone, silk, and bamboo,
as if the music of heaven descended.
Ascending eastern songs,
performing southern tunes.
Continuing Yáng'ē,
singing Mèirèn.
Jīng's beauties and Chǔ's dances,
Wú's joys and Yuè's chants.
Harmonious and graceful,
gentle and serene.
"Such as these,
with the grand echoes of call and response,
moving bells and drums with resonant clangs.
Like a massive mound collapsing ahead,
the melody's twists hard to surpass.
All harmonizing with folk songs,
pitches and tones in mutual accord.
When the music plays,
even wood and stone take on luster;
when it expresses sorrow,
then fierce winds suddenly arise.
Some surpass Yánlù and Jiàbiàn,
some exceed Lǜshuǐ and Cǎilíng.
Army horses lower manes and raise heads to listen,
deep-water fish raise scales and rise upward.
Merriment half-done,
eight tones combined.
Joyful feelings linger,
fine hours proceed.
Lǔ Yáng brandishes his spear and raises high his banner,
turning back the shining sun to the great clarity.
About to shift the western sun to midday again,
matching the past's utmost sincerity.
"In ancient times, the Xiàhòu clan assembled ministers in this land,
and those holding jade and silk numbered ten thousand states.
It was also where former kings held grand gatherings,
and where the four directions followed as a model.
During the Spring and Autumn period,
the lords of key alliances.
Hélǘ trusted in his might,
Fūchāi exhausted his martial prowess.
Internally implementing Wǔ Yuán's strategies,
externally deploying Sūnzǐ's marvels.
Defeated mighty Chǔ at Bǎijǔ,
cornered strong Yuè at Kuàijī.
Dug canals to Shāng and Lǔ,
vied for supremacy at Huángchí.
Merely relying on rivers and lakes as barriers,
abundant in produce and resources.
Ràoliù cannot speak of its solidity,
Zhèng and Bái cannot describe its abundance.
The men possess the sharpness to break through fortifications,
the customs uphold a spirit of integrity.
At a glare of anger, they draw swords;
at a growl of rage, they bend bows.
Those who hold it soar like dragons,
those who occupy it glare like tigers.
Sweeping cities like shaking dead leaves,
capturing flags like glancing and pointing.
Though armored but for a morning,
yet great achievements reach far.
Though generations accumulate a hundredfold,
yet wealth and strength succeed one another.
Joy and prosperity flourish in this region,
immortals gather upon this land.
Guìfǔ refined his form and changed his appearance,
Chìxū shed his skin and attached himself here.
Within central Xià compared to this,
throughout ages rarely seen,
paintings depict its treasures and wonders,
valuing its precious benefits.
Shùn and Yǔ traveled here,
forgetting to return till the end of their days,
spirits linger in its mountain recesses,
delighting in its strange beauty.
Analyzing the multitude of lands,
deliberating on the myriad customs.
States may have oppressive gloom yet appear open,
nations may have cramped narrowness and curl up constrained.
But this capital's vastness,
encompasses Shénzhōu and stores treasures.
Looking up to the Southern Dipper to measure,
blessed with the excellence of both heaven and earth.
"Judging from this,
the difference between Western Shǔ and Eastern Wú,
in terms of their vast disparity,
is like comparing the glow of fireflies in a thorny forest
to the brilliance of a dragon-shaped candle on a sandalwood tree.
The opposition between adversity and prosperity,
is like the liberation of a deity,
compared to the shackles of confinement.
How can one discuss greatness and pettiness in the same era,
or debate abundance and barrenness in the same year?
As for their secluded and profound depths,
vast and tranquil mysteries,
where the ears and eyes cannot perceive,
and the feet and toes cannot tread,
the utmost peculiarities of the extraordinary,
the strange and bizarre occurrences,
hidden principles since ancient times,
yet unawakened by earlier insights.
As for what you, my friend, have transmitted,
the reckless remnants of words,
merely outlining the generalities,
without grasping the essential subtleties."
The gentleman from the state of Wèi, with a dignified countenance,
raised his gaze and proclaimed:
"How different are the scholars of Jiāo and Yì!
For sounds vary between Chǔ and Xià,
due to the divergence of local customs;
temperaments range from treacherous to easygoing,
because of the differences in habits.
Although these are inherent,
they are certainly not what we call self-attained.
In the past, Shìnán Yìliáo juggled balls,
and the conflicts between two families were resolved.
Allow me, for your sake, to revisit the virtuous words,
to settle the debate between the two guests in the arena of argument."
"When the Great Ultimate divided,
creation began its course.
Its substance encompasses day and night,
its principle contains purity and turbidity.
Flowing, it becomes rivers and seas;
congealing, it forms mountains and peaks.
The constellations divide the regions,
the remote borders encircle the corners.
Cliffs, ridges, deep pools, and abysses,
separate the barbarians and the Yi tribes,
are the perilous passes.
The settlements of the Mán and Yí tribes,
accessible only through interpreters and guides,
are the dwellings of bird-like and beast-like people.
Those who hold the correct position and embody the body,
regard the Central Xià as the throat,
not the borderlands as the lapel.
Those who govern the world and nurture the people,
take morality as their fence,
not reliance on perilous terrain as their screen.
Yet you, a worthy gentleman,
still fail to align with the multitude and equalize authority,
attaching yourself to the imperial standard.
You think of receiving the correct calendar,
and gladly offer tribute and service.
Instead, you merely pursue deceitful followers and unworthy men,
finding comfort in remote lands.
You take pride in your tattooed bodies,
and boast of your perilous thorns.
You confuse the constant norms of silence and speech,
dragging along stubborn words to excess and extravagance.
Adorned with flowery deviations to show off,
pretending to be obstinate and raising your arms in defiance.
Not in the prime of pure essence,
you plot contradictions to royal righteousness.
How is this better than searching for fine grass in the middle of the road,
or creating a monkey from a thorn?
Although Jiàngé is lofty,
those who rely on it will stumble,
for it is not the means to deepen roots and secure foundations.
Although Dòngtíng is deep,
those who bear it will be defeated,
for it is not the way to love people and govern the state.
That last light of the mulberry and elm,
surpasses the first glow of the evening star.
How much more the clear and high lands of Héjì,
compared to the low and damp banks of the Jiāngjiè.
Therefore, I shall tell you of the expanse of the Divine Land,
the borders of the Red County.
The outstanding prominence of the Wèi capital,
the pivotal hub of the six directions."
"At that time, fate encountered the ninth yang,
the Hàn dynasty's net lost its cords.
Treachery and rebellion surged within,
warfare entangled the Purple Palace.
The majestic capital city,
the awe-inspiring imperial domain,
nests burned and plains scorched,
turned into ashes and embers,
hence thorns and brambles grew in the courtyards.
Throughout the vast land,
in all eight regions continuously,
spearheads and arrows crisscrossed,
transformed into battlefields,
hence deer and elk dwelled in the cities.
Yīluò became overgrown and desolate,
Xiáohán lay barren and wild.
Línzī was desolate and sparse,
Yānyǐng reduced to mounds and ruins.
And at this time, when the state of Wèi began its founding days,
at the dawn of its establishment,
compared to the myriad cities,
it was like the difference between an ugly man and the handsome Zǐdū,
or a small mound and the lofty Fāng Hú."
"Moreover, the land of Wèi,
corresponds to the constellations Bì and Mǎo,
inhabited by descendants of Yú and Xià.
The mulberry and catalpa of the former kings,
the lingering dust of successive sages.
Examining its four corners,
it lies at the center of the eight reaches;
measuring its cold and heat,
it is where frost and dew are evenly distributed.
Bǔ Yǎn, with foresight, praised its prosperity;
Wú Zhá, hearing its songs, admired its customs.
Although it was a declining age,
its abundant virtue was expressed in music;
though over a thousand years have passed,
nostalgia is preserved across distant years.
As for its territory,
it extends to Qí and Qín on the sides,
converging and connecting to Jìdào.
Opening its chest to Yīn and Wèi,
straddling and stepping over Yān and Zhào.
Mountains and forests deep and serene,
rivers and marshes winding and encircling.
Héng and Jié peaks pierce the azure sky,
Hé and Fén rivers vast and shimmering white.
